name: news-article
archetype: Well-built news/editorial article (control site — intended to be clean)

real_problems.problem: The placeholder image files are all identical 1x1 transparent pixels, not real photographs, despite being referenced as meaningful hero images and headshots.
real_problems.why_it_hurts: This is a cosmetic/test-harness artifact (explicitly permitted by the task brief for placeholder assets), not a structural discoverability defect: every fact and figure that matters (headline, byline, dates, body text, figure captions) lives in real crawlable HTML text, not inside the images. The images are decorative/illustrative supplements, not sole carriers of information, so I am not counting this as a genuine finding — flagging it only for transparency.

legitimate_and_traps.aspect: Correction notice appended to the lede article ("Correction, August 30, 2026: An earlier version of this article misstated...")
legitimate_and_traps.why_it_is_fine: This looks like an admission of an error and might superficially read as a quality problem, but transparent, dated correction notices are a hallmark of trustworthy, well-run journalism (matches AP/NYT-style corrections practice) and should never be flagged as a defect — it is a positive signal of editorial rigor, not sloppiness.

legitimate_and_traps.aspect: robots.txt uses a blanket `User-agent: *` / `Allow: /` with no bot-specific blocks (no GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended disallow rules)
legitimate_and_traps.why_it_is_fine: This is the deliberate, correct choice for a discoverability control: the site is not opting out of AI crawling, so assistants should be able to fetch and cite it. Do not flag the absence of AI-bot blocks as a problem, and do not flag the presence of a permissive robots.txt as if it were unusual/suspicious.

legitimate_and_traps.aspect: Empty/decorative visual separators are not used at all; every has substantive alt text describing real photo content (hero shots, headshots)
legitimate_and_traps.why_it_is_fine: There is no decorative image with alt="" in this site to worry about — all images are content images and correctly carry descriptive alt text. Nothing to flag either way; noting this only so the absence of empty-alt usage isn't mistaken for an oversight.

legitimate_and_traps.aspect: datePublished and dateModified differ by a small but real interval (e.g. published 12:12 PM, updated 9:05 AM the next day) rather than being identical or wildly stale
legitimate_and_traps.why_it_is_fine: Identical publish/modify timestamps can be a sign of fabricated freshness, and a modified date far in the future/past can look manipulated. These small, plausible gaps reflect genuine light editing/updating and should read as authentic freshness, not be penalized as inconsistent.

legitimate_and_traps.aspect: Internal navigation only links to pages that actually exist (index.html, articles/texas-battery-co-op-heat-dome.html, author/priya-chandran.html) rather than a full multi-section nav with placeholder sections
legitimate_and_traps.why_it_is_fine: This was a deliberate choice to avoid introducing broken links / 404s in a control site meant to be clean; a real large news site would have many more nav sections, but every link here resolves. This should not be flagged as a 'thin site' problem — it's intentionally scoped to what was built.

legitimate_and_traps.aspect: JSON-LD NewsArticle/ProfilePage structured data is present, valid, and consistent with the visible on-page content (same headline, same author name, same dates)
legitimate_and_traps.why_it_is_fine: This is the correct, expected implementation for a news article and should be recognized as a positive signal (machine-readable author/date/publisher facts matching the human-visible content), not treated with suspicion as 'too perfect.'

legitimate_and_traps.aspect: Content is 100% server-delivered static HTML with no client-side rendering, no JS required to see the article text, headline, byline, or date
legitimate_and_traps.why_it_is_fine: This is correct and intentional: a crawler or assistant fetching the raw HTML gets the full article immediately. Do not expect or require a noscript fallback warning here since there is no JS-gated content at all.

legitimate_and_traps.aspect: author page email and social links (mailto:, linkedin.example, x.example) point to non-resolving example domains
legitimate_and_traps.why_it_is_fine: These are placeholder/example domains consistent with the whole site living on the fictional continentalledger.example domain; this is a natural artifact of building an offline test fixture, not a real dead-link defect a live crawl would encounter on the real internet, so it should not be scored as a broken-link problem.

notes:
Design intent: this is the CONTROL site and was built to have essentially no genuine defects. Structure: index.html is itself the flagship article (not a homepage-with-teasers layout), with a second full article and an author bio page for realistic internal linking, plus robots.txt and sitemap.xml covering all three real URLs.

Discoverability strengths deliberately built in: single canonical URL per page with matching og:url; complete Open Graph + Twitter Card tags; valid schema.org NewsArticle JSON-LD on both articles (headline, image, datePublished, dateModified, author with URL, publisher with logo, mainEntityOfPage) and ProfilePage/Person JSON-LD on the author page; semantic HTML (article/header/figure/figcaption/address/time with machine-readable datetime attributes); a single H1 per page with a clean H2 subhead hierarchy; descriptive, keyword-relevant alt text on every image; permissive robots.txt with an explicit Sitemap directive; a sitemap.xml listing exactly the three real pages with accurate lastmod dates; clear named author with title, bio, contact, and a byline link that round-trips to the author page; consistent NAP-style publisher identity ("The Continental Ledger") across both articles.

Engagement strengths deliberately built in: a real, specific, non-clickbait headline and dek; a visible byline + published/updated timestamps + read-time estimate immediately under the headline; a lede that states the concrete finding in the first sentence; a named, quoted source with attribution context; a genuine cross-link between the two articles ("related coverage") that is contextual and bidirectional; a transparent, dated correction notice (signals editorial trustworthiness rather than being a defect); an author bio page with credentials and a list of recent bylines; no popups, no paywall, no infinite-scroll trickery, no autoplay media — nothing standing between the visitor and the text.

The only thing I flagged at all is that the placeholder image files are 1x1 stand-ins (unavoidable/explicitly sanctioned for this fixture-building exercise) rather than real photos — but since no fact in either article depends on the image (all captions, figures, and claims are in the surrounding text), this does not create an actual discoverability gap, so I rated it low/informational rather than a real problem. I made a deliberate choice to keep the nav scoped only to pages that exist rather than simulate a fuller site with dead links, to avoid accidentally injecting an unintended defect into what is supposed to be the clean control.
